findings.reason: it adds one clause to the ceiling ("less the unspent part of the USD 60 tranche authorised to `sn-catalog-consistency` §2") plus the matching depend-on, and without it the ceiling can read affordable against a balance that is already committed.
findings.text: §5's ceiling is "the spend per name … times the backlog … plus a quarter" against "the approval's remaining balance", and it says "Spend draws on what remains of the USD 350 approval after §4", but §4 (line 53) protects "the unspent part of the USD 60 tranche authorised to `sn-catalog-consistency` §2" and §5 neither deducts it nor declares `sn-catalog-consistency#s2`; since that section is still `implementable` and §5 has no dependency ordering it after that section, a §5 that closes under its ceiling can spend money already authorised elsewhere

response_events.note: Section 5 spend now deducts the unspent part of the consistency section 2 tranche at its start.
